## When asked: "What was the average monthly consumption of customers in SME for the year 2013?"

One row of `yearmonth` = one customer, one month, that month's total consumption. Every row is already a monthly value. So "average monthly consumption" = plain AVG over `Consumption`, one step, done. Do not divide by 12.

Peak month = the month with the highest total consumption: filter customers to `Segment = 'SME'`, filter `Date` to 2013, aggregate per month, order by total descending, take the top one. The month is the 5th-6th characters of `Date` (YYYYMM).

input.sql: SELECT c.Segment, c.Currency, COUNT(*) AS n FROM customers c GROUP BY c.Segment, c.Currency ORDER BY c.Segment
SELECT substr(Date,1,4) AS yr, COUNT(*) AS n FROM yearmonth GROUP BY yr

SELECT c.Segment,
       SUM(CASE WHEN substr(y.Date,1,4)='2012' THEN y.Consumption ELSE 0 END) AS total2012,
       SUM(CASE WHEN substr(y.Date,1,4)='2013' THEN y.Consumption ELSE 0 END) AS total2013,
       CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN substr(y.Date,1,4)='2013' THEN y.Consumption ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN substr(y.Date,1,4)='2012' THEN y.Consumption ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) / SUM(CASE WHEN substr(y.Date,1,4)='2012' THEN y.Consumption ELSE 0 END) * 100 AS pct_increase
FROM yearmonth y JOIN customers c ON y.CustomerID = c.CustomerID
WHERE c.Currency='EUR' AND substr(y.Date,1,4) IN ('2012','2013')
GROUP BY c.Segment
